resources.string: Lets you select words anywhere on your screen to translate them, without Android asking each time. It only takes a screenshot when you tap the Select on screen tile, this feature\'s shortcut or its Capture button. While you continue a selection, it notices how far apps scroll, to keep the selection marked. It can\'t read the content of other apps, and screenshots stay in memory on your phone.
Read the whole image with the vision model
Plus pen. Tap again to change its width.
Minus pen. Tap again to change its width.
Area pen: read a region with the vision model
The text scan didn\'t work. The area pen can still read a region.
This app doesn\'t allow its screen to be captured.
No text found. Try the area pen for anything the scan can\'t read.
Couldn\'t find where the last part ended on this screen.
No text was found in the image.
No API key is set, so the translation was cancelled.
Fetch and select a model in Settings, or enter a model ID.
[No API key is set; can\'t back-translate]
The source and the translation are in the same language; there\'s nothing to back-translate.
Android asks you to confirm the update. The first time, it also asks you to let SnipDo install apps.
Allow SnipDo to install apps, then tap Install again.
The downloaded file isn\'t a valid update for this app, so it was deleted.

Add the Select on screen tile to Quick Settings, then tap it on any screen. Each time, Android asks whether to share the screen with SnipDo: tap Start or Share screen. You can also take a screenshot and share it to SnipDo.
SnipDo takes one screenshot and stops capturing straight away. The screenshot stays in memory on this phone. Nothing is sent until you confirm, and then only the words you selected.
On. The tile captures without asking. If you also turned on the SnipDo screen selection shortcut in Accessibility settings, its floating button or gesture starts a selection from any screen.

Off. Turn on SnipDo screen selection in Accessibility settings and the tile captures without asking. You can also turn on its shortcut there: a floating button or gesture that starts a selection from any screen. Whenever the service is off, the tile asks as above.

If Android says it\'s a restricted setting, open App info, tap the ⋮ menu, choose Allow restricted settings, and try again. Some phones, such as Xiaomi, turn the service off when SnipDo is cleared from recent apps; the tile then asks each time until you turn it back on.

The service can only take a screenshot, only when you tap the tile, its shortcut or Capture, and can\'t read other apps\' content. While you continue a selection, it notices how far the app scrolls, to keep the selection marked.
Added “%1$s” to Quick Settings. New tiles usually go on the last page. To move it, open Quick Settings and tap the pencil (Edit) button.
“%1$s” is already in Quick Settings, on the last page unless you\'ve moved it. To move it, open Quick Settings and tap the pencil (Edit) button.
“%1$s” wasn\'t added. To add it yourself, open Quick Settings, tap the pencil (Edit) button and drag it into your tiles.
Every provider uses the OpenAI Chat Completions format. API keys are encrypted and stored per provider on this phone.
%1$s: enter a valid HTTPS base URL and model ID. The base URL can\'t contain a key, query or fragment.
%1$s: that API key can\'t be used.
The API key couldn\'t be saved on this phone.
Everyone speaks this language, so there\'s nothing to translate.

This phone has no speech recognition service, so SnipDo can\'t hear the speakers. Install or turn on one, such as Speech Recognition and Synthesis from Google, or, if your model accepts audio, turn on Supports audio input in Settings → Translation service.
SnipDo needs the microphone to hear the speakers. Allow it in App info → Permissions.
%1$s, which does speech recognition on this phone, isn\'t allowed to use the microphone, so it can\'t hear the speakers. Allow the microphone in its App info → Permissions.
The microphone isn\'t available. Another app may be using it.

Speech recognition on this phone can\'t hear %1$s. If your model accepts audio, turn on Supports audio input in Settings → Translation service to hear it through the model. Until then, this speaker still gets translations into %1$s.
To hear %1$s, SnipDo sends the speech to your model. That needs an API key, a model, and Supports audio input turned on in Settings → Translation service.
Your model couldn\'t write down what was said: %1$s
Can\'t be heard on this phone
Speech recognition couldn\'t reach its service. Check the connection and try again.
Speech recognition stopped working. Try again.
Stopped listening after a minute without speech.
This phone has no voice for %1$s, so it isn\'t read aloud.
Add your API key and choose a model
Open Quick Settings and tap it over any app
Add the Select on screen tile to Quick Settings
Choose each speaker\'s language above their button.
Tap a button to talk and tap it again to stop, or hold it while you talk.
Each sentence is translated for the other speakers, and read aloud when Read aloud is on.
Add it from the Quick Settings editor
One screenshot per tap, kept in memory on this phone. Only the words you select are sent.
This removes every saved translation from this phone.
